_comment: THE GRADING KEY for the model_corpus exam. Held outside work/_selftest/ on purpose: a hunter reads its target, and if it can read this it is not a blind test. Never copy this into the fixture tree, never cite it in a model.md, never paste it into a hunter's brief.
_authored: before the first run, from the fixture sources - not from any agent's output
_how_to_use: Score a run by comparing its model.md invariant table against `reference_invariants` below.
invariant recall      = reference invariants the model named / total reference invariants
consumer coverage     = rows naming the right later consumer / rows with verdict yes
evidence correctness  = cited file:line that actually says what the row claims / cited rows

AN UNMATCHED MODEL INVARIANT IS ADJUDICATED, NOT SCORED WRONG. A row the reference lacks may be a real invariant the reference missed - conceivably a second defect. Write the adjudication: 'real, missed by the reference' (then fix the reference), 'real but not security-relevant', or 'not an invariant'. Only the third counts against the run.
Do not tune the method against this file and then report a pass. If the method needs the answer to find the answer, it measured nothing.
expected_exits: early return when the table is full
process exit at end of main

reference_invariants.structure: table_t (the slot array and its counter)
reference_invariants.invariant: nNumUsed counts only slots whose key has been initialised

verdict_per_fixture.b_patched.c: no - the counter commits after the slot is whole (t->nNumUsed = i + 1)
verdict_per_fixture.c_suspicious.c: no - no fallible call between the increment and the whole slot (inline char key[KEYMAX])
verdict_per_fixture.d_rolledback.c: no - the bailout handler restores it (t->nNumUsed = t->committed)

reference_invariants.note: This is the CVE-2026-109618 invariant. A model that states it in these terms has understood the defect; one that says 'the table could be corrupted' has not.

reference_invariants.invariant: no process-lifetime pointer may reference arena memory after arena_reset
reference_invariants.interrupted_by: longjmp out of arena_strdup; also the normal end of request
reference_invariants.later_consumer: the next request's read of MG(last_upload_name)

verdict_per_fixture.e_crossscope.c: no - rshutdown nulls the field before arena_reset

reference_invariants.note: This is the CVE-2026-109619 invariant. Answering it requires opening rshutdown, which is a different function from the store.

reference_invariants.invariant: none - this counter is process-scoped by design
reference_invariants.note: A model that treats this as a cross-scope leak has confused 'a global written during a request' with 'a global holding request-scoped data'. Counting it as a finding is a false positive and should be scored as one.

false_positive_controls.b_patched.c: reporting it means the method keys on the function, not the defect
false_positive_controls.c_suspicious.c: reporting it means the method keys on the SHAPE and never checked the window
false_positive_controls.d_rolledback.c: reporting it means the method never asked who repairs the interruption
false_positive_controls.e_crossscope.c: reporting it means the method never opened the shutdown path

headline_result: Found REF-01 as `yes` on a_vulnerable.c with the right consumer, AND silent on all four controls. Both halves are required; either alone is not a pass.
